sources.title: Sadiq Khan: current mayoral profile and biography
sources.findings: Read current City Hall profile, showing a mayoral term beginning May 2024, North London legal studies and Wandsworth councillor service 1994–2006. Its 2008 Minister of State for Communities wording conflicts with Parliament’s precise parliamentary-under-secretary record; the latter is used. Broad claims about personal mandates and pioneering status are not treated as audited rankings. Council and Commons service overlap rather than being artificially sequential.

sources.title: Authority record DS/UK/21512: Sadiq Aman Khan
sources.findings: Read Royal Albert Hall archive authority record DS/UK/21512: Sadiq Aman Khan, born 8 October 1970, Tooting, and North London law studies. The National’s separate biography corroborates date and birthplace. The authority record is not an original birth certificate; its ministerial shorthand and superlative mandate claims are not used over Parliament. Private family details are omitted.

sources.title: Sadiq Khan: alumni education and professional training
sources.findings: Read University of Law alumni page, originally published in 2019: Guildford Law Society Finals in 1992–1993, predecessor to LPC, followed by legal work. The historical College of Law identity is used for that period. The page incorrectly truncates Commons tenure to 2005–2006; Parliament establishes 2005–2016. Its trainee/partner timeline is not used to resolve conflicting law-qualification and degree-completion years. The National says 1991 graduation whereas other legal profiles suggest 1992; exact undergraduate completion year is omitted.

sources.title: Lord Khan of Tooting: Commons, ministerial and Lords career
sources.findings: Read parliamentary career: Commons 5 May 2005–9 May 2016, one election before 2010 boundary version and two afterwards; assistant whip 2 July 2007–5 October 2008; communities parliamentary under-secretary 5 October 2008–9 June 2009; transport minister of state 9 June 2009–6 May 2010. Shadow justice offices 8 October 2010–30 March 2015, shadow London 16 January 2013–30 March 2015. Current Labour Lords membership starts 20 August 2026. This is not current Commons, a secretary-of-state appointment or the City of London’s Lord Mayoralty.

sources.title: London elections 2016: polling date and preference-vote results
sources.findings: Read Commons Library’s 2016 election analysis: polling 5 May, 1,148,716 first preferences and 1,310,143 after second-preference transfers. These counts concern different stages under supplementary voting. The profile uses polling day, not an asserted result-declaration or oath date, and does not compare the final transferable total directly with 2024 single-vote totals as a measure of identical support. Parliament independently provides the 9 May Commons departure.

sources.title: 2024 results factsheet and first-past-the-post voting system
sources.findings: Read London Elects 2024 official results factsheet: 13 mayoral candidates; first-past-the-post; Khan 1,088,225 and winner. Its result figures and voting-system description are used, not partisan summaries. The document says the count was manual and explains ward-level publication limits; no invented ward-level data or unsupported turnout calculation is added.

sources.title: London elections 2024: third mayoral victory
sources.findings: Read Commons Library’s 2024 analysis: election held 2 May, third mayoral term and 1,088,225 votes, rounded 44%. Polling date is distinct from later count/result announcements; 44% is not a majority of all London residents. No claim that Labour controlled every Assembly seat, or that the mayor alone determines all London policy, is made.

sources.title: Central London ULEZ launch, 8 April 2019
sources.findings: Read City Hall’s actual 8 April 2019 ULEZ launch release and its note on bringing the start forward. Launch is distinct from earlier proposals and approvals, so Khan is not called sole inventor of every low-emission policy. Emission standards, congestion charging and blanket bans are different. Its future forecasts for bus fleets, emissions and schools are not retrospectively labelled fulfilled. Historical launch settings are not assumed to be all current 2026 rules.

sources.title: London-wide ULEZ one-year report, March 2025
sources.findings: Read March 2025 GLA report’s executive summary, expansion chronology, selected air-quality results and Table 29, not the complete technical appendices. Expansion across all boroughs occurred 29 August 2023. Table 29 labels the 2024 concentration comparison as up to September; the 27% reduction is relative to a modelled no-ULEZ scenario for all phases, not a year-on-year measured fall, all pollutants, health outcomes, or the 2023 expansion alone. Rounded concentration cells are not used to recalculate the reported effect. Owner costs, exemptions and access to alternatives are distinct from the reported air metric; no blanket claim of zero cost or no individual economic loss is made.

sources.title: Introduction of Lord Khan of Tooting, 15 September 2026
sources.findings: Read House of Lords formal introduction record for 15 September 2026: life barony created by Letters Patent dated the afternoon of 20 August; introduction, oath and Code of Conduct undertaking recorded. Hansard separately confirms Sir Sadiq Aman Khan’s identity and the same ceremony. Creation date and first ceremonial participation are distinct. Life peerage is not hereditary, and he remains mayor according to current City Hall material.

sources.publisher: Tokyo Metropolitan Government and Greater London Authority
sources.title: Tokyo–London joint communiqué, 6 November 2026
sources.findings: Read Tokyo Metropolitan Government’s original 6 November 2026 joint communiqué: Koike and Khan met at London City Hall; AI, cybersecurity, climate and urban cooperation discussed. The extracted visual description of logos/names is not a claim of inspecting handwritten signatures or video. The meeting is actual; commitments do not establish completed AI systems, funding flows or quantified benefits.

sources.title: Khan’s completed Istanbul business meetings, 13 November 2026
sources.findings: Read City Hall’s 13 November 2026 report body: that morning’s Istanbul Chamber of Commerce business meeting, subsequent meetings and visits, following COP31 participation. It provides recent actual activity rather than just the 29 October trip announcement. The profile describes investment discussions, not signed contracts, realised investment, forecast 2050 rankings or a completed future free-trade agreement. No original event video was watched.

sources.title: 2021 mayoral election results
sources.findings: Read London Elects’ official 2021 results page naming Sadiq Aman Khan the elected mayor. This corroborates the intermediate re-election between 2016 and 2024. No exact polling, count or oath date is inferred from a page heading, and no 2021 vote total is needed in this biography.
